ns2:section.sectionText: Topic: Graduate seminar on Distributed cognition and interactive behavior This seminar will include theories and empirical research focuses on situations in which cognition is not confined to the individual, but distributed across individuals and/or objects in our environment. Interactive behavior is defined as the patterns of activities that emerge from the co-ordination between individuals and artifacts in various complex socio-technological systems. Topics will include how characteristics of the environment may interact with low-level perceptual-motor and cognitive operations and higher level behavior such as learning, information-seeking, and decision making at both the individual and social levels. Implications to designs of interactive environments will be discussed.
